headline: Math nears saturation while real-world agent work remains the slow frontier
outlook: Over the past year math has closed 95% of its remaining headroom, with FrontierMath and ARC-AGI-2 both passing 90% this summer. Agents and real work have closed only 34%, leaving the Remote Labor Index at 21.2% and OSWorld 2 at 31.4%. That gap is starting to narrow at the edges. APEX-Agents climbed from 68.6% to 82.4% across three releases in September, and the length of task models can handle, now 17.4 hours for Claude Mythos Preview, is doubling roughly every 4.1 months, which on current trends puts a full 40-hour work-week most likely around December, though the range runs into August 2027. Meanwhile the price of strong GPQA performance has fallen from $3.44 per million tokens with Gemini 2.5 Pro to $0.055 with Qwen3.7 Flash, a trend of about 24 times cheaper per year. Not everything follows the curves: Terminal-Bench and GeoBench have stalled short of 90% months after their fits said they would arrive, and past likely ranges caught the real date only 59% of the time, so the open question for the coming year is whether long, messy real-world work keeps pace with the task-horizon trend or stalls the way those benchmarks have.
